players.product: electrical distributor - transformer buyer (HICO America customer)

quarterly_data.signal: Record first quarter: reported sales of $6.1 billion, up 14% year-over-year including 12% organic growth (third quarter in a row of double-digit sales growth), with volume growth across all three SBUs and an estimated price benefit of approximately 3 points. Adjusted EBITDA increased 25% to $389 million with margin up 60 basis points to 6.4%; adjusted EPS rose 52% to $3.37; free cash flow was $213 million, 128% of adjusted net income.
quarterly_data.figure: sales $6.1 billion, +14% (12% organic); adjusted EBITDA $389 million, 6.4% margin; adjusted EPS $3.37 (+52%); free cash flow $213 million

quarterly_data.signal: Data center sales reached approximately $1.4 billion, up about 70% year-over-year and 24% of total company sales in the quarter; data center is now Wesco's largest end market across all three SBUs (CSS white space, EES gray space, UBS grid services power solutions), serving hyperscale, multi-tenant, colocation and enterprise customers. On a trailing 12-month basis data center sales are approximately $4.8 billion, or 20% of total sales.
quarterly_data.figure: data center sales $1.4 billion, up approximately 70%, 24% of sales; trailing 12-month approximately $4.8 billion or 20% of sales

quarterly_data.signal: Record backlog, up 22% year-over-year - growing faster than sales at every SBU: CSS backlog up approximately 40% (driven by data center project activity), EES up 14% (with double-digit backlog growth in industrial) and UBS up 16%. Management says a number of backlog projects ship in 2027, and it is quoting longer-lead items for 2027 and 2028, 'like some transformer business and utility'; multi-year alliance agreements are loaded only as POs arrive.

CSS (Communications & Security Solutions) organic sales grew 22% (reported 24%), driven by Wesco Data Center Solutions, which had a record quarter with sales up over 60% (white space growth 'north of 60%'); volume up about 21%, price approximately 1%. Enterprise network infrastructure declined mid-single digits on service provider weakness but grew high teens including data center sales. Adjusted EBITDA rose 41% to $223 million with margin up 110 basis points to 9%; management says despite modest gross margin pressure from large data center projects, Wesco Data Center Solutions margins are healthy and accretive.
quarterly_data.figure: CSS organic sales +22% (reported +24%); data center solutions sales up over 60%; adjusted EBITDA $223 million, 9% margin

quarterly_data.signal: EES (Electrical & Electronic Solutions) organic sales grew 7% (reported 9%); OEM was up mid-teens on strength in the semiconductor and data center markets and construction up low double digits on wire and cable demand, while industrial was down low single digits on project timing. EES data center (gray space) sales were up over 100% year-over-year and about 10% of EES sales; management says the majority of this gray-space growth was not linked to a prior CSS white-space win. Adjusted EBITDA rose 30% to $185 million, margin 8.2%.
quarterly_data.figure: EES organic sales +7%; EES data center sales up over 100%, about 10% of EES sales; OEM up mid-teens; adjusted EBITDA $185 million, 8.2% margin

quarterly_data.signal: UBS (Utility & Broadband Solutions) delivered 6% organic growth: utility up high single digits on strong double-digit growth in investor-owned utilities and grid services momentum, public power flat, broadband up mid-single digits. Gross margins are expected to remain under pressure given weak sales in transformers and wire and cable; adjusted EBITDA was $131 million (down 5%), margin 9.6%. Management reports increasing interest in its grid services-enabled power capabilities from hyperscalers and other data center customers and a growing funnel of opportunities.
quarterly_data.figure: UBS organic sales +6%; adjusted EBITDA $131 million, 9.6% margin

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 outlook raised: reported sales growth of 6%-9% and organic growth of 5%-8%, implying reported sales of approximately $24.9 billion-$25.6 billion; adjusted EBITDA margin 6.6%-7% (unchanged, higher in dollars); adjusted EPS raised to $15-$17; free cash flow $500 million-$800 million. CSS outlook raised to low double-digit growth, with data center sales now expected up 20%+ for the year (management attributes the back-half step-down to project timing); EES and UBS outlooks unchanged. Q2: April month-to-date sales per workday up about 10%, Q2 reported sales expected up high single digits, EBITDA margin about flat with roughly 25 basis points of incentive-compensation headwind.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 reported sales +6%-9%, organic +5%-8% ($24.9 billion-$25.6 billion); EBITDA margin 6.6%-7%; adjusted EPS $15-$17; data center sales up 20%+; April sales per workday up about 10%

quarterly_data.signal: Supply constraints: asked about long switchgear lead times, the CEO said the analyst's lead-time comments are accurate and that Wesco still sees extended lead times in two critical categories, which it has managed since the pandemic; the CFO said the throttling factors for building infrastructure are lead time and skilled labor, not appetite for investment or capital allocation. The CEO sees the beginning of an industrial super cycle driven by AI infrastructure, power generation needs and reshoring, and Wesco is making facility and capability expansion investments to support data center growth.

Pricing: the approximately 3-point price benefit was mostly carryover from prior-year increases; by SBU price contributed approximately 1% in CSS, about 4% in EES and about 3% in UBS. Management notes CSS is now its largest business unit with a smaller price impact, and an increasing share of projects use negotiated special pricing agreements; tariff impact is not material and transportation cost increases are being passed to customers where appropriate.
quarterly_data.figure: price approximately 3 points; CSS approximately 1%, EES about 4%, UBS about 3%
